title_ar: الشيخ الددو يؤكد في خطبة الجمعة على نصرة الشعب السوري والوقوف معه في محنته
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Affirms in his Friday Sermon the Necessity of Supporting the Syrian People and Standing with Them in Their Ordeal
body_ar:
أكد الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء في خطبته للجمعة بجامع أسامة أمس 15 اكتوبر 2011 على ضرورة نصرة الشعب السوري والوقوف معه في محنته التي لا تزال مستمرة منذ أشهر، وحذر فضيلة الشيخ من الظلم وعواقبه الوخيمة وقال حفظه الله: "في هذا الزمان نرى الكثير من فشو الظلم والأخذ به، وقد شاهدنا ظلم الأجانب للمسلمين لكن الذى أنكى من ذلك وأوجع أن يعتدى من يعتبر نفسه من المسلمين على المسلمين والعالم يتفرج".

ويأتي هذا التأكيد من الشيخ – حفظه الله- على النصرة للشعب السوري استجابة لنداء الاتحاد العالمي لعلماء المسلمين الذى أعلن هذا اليوم الجمعة يوما للتضامن مع الشعب السوري المنكوب .

وقال حفظه الله: إن الذى يحصل الآن في سوريا يدمي القلب ولابد من إنكاره ومن شأن المؤمن إذا ضيم أي مسلم أن يتحرك قلبه لذلك، ثم ذكر الحاكم في سوريا ومن ورائه كل الظالمين قائلا: إنك زائل لامحالة ولو دامت لغيرك ما وصلت إليك .

ونبه الشيخ – حفظه الله – الحكام وولاة الأمور وكل من طغى وتجبر إلى أن الغفلة عن أخذ الله الوبيل هي أصل كثير من الأدواء وأن الله يمهل ولا يهمل..

وختم هذه الخطبة بدعاء شامل وبليغ.

لمتابعة الخطبة اضغط هنا.
body_en:
In his Friday sermon at the Usamah Mosque yesterday, 15 October 2011, Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, affirmed the necessity of supporting the Syrian people and of standing with them in their ordeal, which has now continued for months. His Eminence the Sheikh warned against oppression and its grievous consequences, and said, may God preserve him: "In this age we see much spreading of oppression and much taking to it. We have seen the oppression of foreigners towards the Muslims; but what is more galling and more painful than that is that one who counts himself among the Muslims should assault Muslims while the world stands by watching."

This affirmation by the Sheikh, may God preserve him, of support for the Syrian people comes in response to the call of the International Union of Muslim Scholars, which declared this Friday a day of solidarity with the stricken Syrian people.

He said, may God preserve him: what is happening now in Syria makes the heart bleed and must be rejected, and it is the way of a believer that when any Muslim is wronged his heart is stirred at it. He then mentioned the ruler in Syria, and behind him all oppressors, saying: you will pass away, inevitably; had it endured for another, it would never have come to you.

And the Sheikh, may God preserve him, alerted the rulers and those in authority and everyone who has been tyrannical and overbearing to the fact that heedlessness of God's grievous seizing is the root of many ills, and that God grants respite but does not neglect.

And he closed this sermon with a comprehensive and eloquent supplication.

flags.arabic: ثم ذكر الحاكم في سوريا ومن ورائه كل الظالمين قائلا: إنك زائل لامحالة
options: translate faithfully and hold for an editorial decision
flags.note: editorial_review. Style guide section 12. A named scholar addressing a sitting head of state in a Friday sermon to tell him he will inevitably fall, and calling for support of a people in revolt against him. Translated faithfully, neither softened nor strengthened. In Arabic in October 2011 this is homiletic and of a piece with the sermons of many scholars that month; in English, standing alone on a website, it is a political statement by a living person about a still-living head of state, and both its republication and its attribution carry exposure. The decision whether and how to publish belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office. This record and record 754 in this same span are two reports of the same campaign and should be weighed together.

flags.arabic: في خطبته للجمعة … أمس 15 اكتوبر 2011 … أعلن هذا اليوم الجمعة يوما للتضامن
options: reproduce the date exactly as given and flag it
flags.note: The date does not fit. 15 October 2011 was a Saturday; the Friday was 14 October. The report is timestamped Sunday 16 October and says the sermon was 'yesterday', which would be the Saturday, while also calling it the Friday sermon and referring to 'this Friday' as the Union's day of solidarity. At least one of the three is wrong. Nothing has been corrected, per style guide section 11; a reviewer should settle the date from the recording before the record is displayed.

flags.arabic: إنك زائل لامحالة ولو دامت لغيرك ما وصلت إليك
flags.context: the words addressed to the ruler in Syria
options: you will pass away, inevitably; had it endured for another, it would never have come to you
you will certainly be gone; if power had lasted for anyone else it would never have reached you
your end is certain; had it been permanent for others, it would not have passed to you
flags.note: The second clause is a proverb about the impermanence of power, and its subject is not stated in the Arabic — 'it' is power or rule, understood. English forces a choice. Option 1 keeps the subject unstated as the Arabic does; option 2 supplies 'power', which is certainly the sense but is an insertion. Given what the sentence is and to whom it is addressed, the translator has preferred not to add a word.

flags.arabic: ونبه … إلى أن الغفلة عن أخذ الله الوبيل هي أصل كثير من الأدواء
flags.note: أخذ الله is the Qur'anic 'seizing' (as in 'the seizing of your Lord is severe'), and الوبيل is its adjective in Sūrat al-Muzzammil 73:16. The phrase is not presented as a quotation and is not marked as one; the Qur'anic register is carried by keeping 'seizing' rather than substituting a plainer word for punishment.

translator_notes: This is a news report of a sermon, written by the site's news desk. Only the first quotation is given inside quotation marks; the rest is reported speech, and how close it is to the Sheikh's wording cannot be determined from this record. The sermon itself exists as audio at the link recorded.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the report was written. The body's own date is internally inconsistent — see the flag.

No ruling word appears anywhere in this record. ضرورة in the first sentence is the reporter's word for the urgency of the call and is not the technical ḍarūrah of the glossary, which is a threshold with a defined legal effect; it is rendered 'necessity' in its ordinary sense and takes no part in the five-rulings mapping.
الاتحاد العالمي لعلماء المسلمين is rendered by the body's own English name, the International Union of Muslim Scholars.
Compare record 754 in this span, a fuller report of the same campaign of sermons on Syria, which carries its own editorial_review flags.
The closing 'to follow the sermon click here' is the site's navigation furniture; preserved in body_ar, recorded in source_download_link, omitted from body_en.
